title: Chicken Caesar Salad
description: Keep the dressing and croutons apart from the leaves and this survives a night in the fridge. Dressed, it does not.
steps: Toss the bread cubes with 2 tbsp of the oil and bake at 200°C for 10 minutes until crisp.
Season the chicken and pan-fry in the remaining oil for 6 minutes a side. Rest, then slice.
Mash the anchovies with the garlic, then whisk with the yoghurt, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Toss the lettuce with the dressing, chicken, croutons and parmesan.
To store: leaves, chicken, croutons and dressing in four parts, combined only at the table.

title: Tuna and White Bean Salad
description: No cooking at all. Because the beans hold the dressing rather than wilting in it, this one actually keeps two days.
steps: Soak the sliced onion in the vinegar for 10 minutes to take the raw edge off it.
Combine the beans, tuna, tomatoes and capers in a bowl.
Add the onion with its vinegar, the oil and the lemon juice, and fold gently so the tuna stays in flakes.
Season well and stir the parsley through.

title: Greek Chicken Wrap
description: The obvious home for last night's roast or grilled chicken. Assemble in the morning and it holds until lunch.
steps: Toss the chicken with the oil and oregano and pan-fry 8 minutes until cooked through.
Squeeze the water out of the grated cucumber, then mix with the yoghurt, garlic and dill.
Spread the tzatziki over each tortilla.
Add chicken, tomato, onion and feta and roll tightly, folding one end in.
Wrap in paper and press for a few minutes so it holds together.

title: Haloumi and Chickpea Salad
description: Fried haloumi over spiced chickpeas. Meat-free, high protein, and the chickpea base keeps three days on its own.
steps: Toss the chickpeas with 1 tbsp of the oil and the spices and roast at 220°C for 20 minutes until they crackle.
Fry the haloumi in a dry hot pan for 2 minutes a side until deeply browned.
Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, onion and herbs with the remaining oil and lemon juice.
Fold the warm chickpeas through and lay the haloumi on top.

title: Vietnamese Chicken Noodle Salad
description: Cold noodles, poached chicken and a sharp lime dressing. Eaten straight from the fridge, so it makes an easy desk lunch.
steps: Poach the chicken in barely simmering salted water for 12 minutes, then rest and shred.
Soak the noodles in hot water until soft, then rinse under cold water and drain very well.
Whisk the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and garlic into a dressing.
Toss everything together with the herbs.
To store: keep the dressing separate; noodles absorb it and turn heavy overnight.

title: Roast Vegetable and Couscous Salad
description: Roasted vegetables folded through couscous. No leaves to wilt, so it holds two days without complaint.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss all the vegetables with 3 tbsp of the oil and the cumin and roast 35 minutes.
Pour the boiling stock over the couscous, cover, and leave 5 minutes. Fork through with the remaining oil.
Fold the hot vegetables and all their tray juices through the couscous.
Add the lemon juice, feta, parsley and almonds.

title: Egg and Avocado Toast
description: Five minutes. Avocado browns within the hour, so this is strictly a make-it-now dish.
steps: Boil the eggs for 7 minutes for a set white and a soft yolk, then cool under cold water and peel.
Toast the bread.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and plenty of salt and spread it thickly.
Halve the eggs over the top, then add the oil and chilli flakes.

title: Caprese Sandwich
description: Four ingredients and no cooking. Salt the tomato first or the bread goes soggy by midday.
steps: Salt the tomato slices and leave them on paper for 5 minutes, then pat dry.
Drizzle the bread with the oil and vinegar.
Layer the mozzarella, tomato and basil and season well.
Press the sandwich under a plate for a few minutes before wrapping.

title: Sesame Chicken Slaw
description: Cabbage stands up to dressing far better than lettuce, so this is one of the few salads that is genuinely better on day two.
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar, honey and ginger into a dressing.
Toss the cabbage and carrot through it and leave 10 minutes to soften slightly.
Fold the chicken, spring onion and coriander through.
Finish with sesame seeds.

title: Bean and Cheese Burrito
description: Roll four at once, wrap them in foil, and reheat one a day. Meat-free and costs almost nothing.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic and spices.
Add the beans with a splash of water and mash about half of them.
Season with lime juice and plenty of salt.
Spread beans, rice and cheese down the middle of each tortilla, fold the ends in and roll tightly.
Toast seam-side down in a dry pan for 2 minutes to seal.

title: Greek Lemon Lentil Soup
description: Six lunches from a bag of lentils. Sharp with lemon, thick by day two, and reheats in two minutes.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 12 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomato paste and oregano and cook 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, stock and bay and simmer 30 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the lemon juice off the heat — added early it stops the lentils softening.
Finish with parsley.

title: Tuna and Capsicum Empanada Bake
description: One big pastry slab instead of fiddly individual parcels. Cuts into six squares and travels well.
steps: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 15 minutes until completely collapsed.
Add the garlic, paprika and tomato paste, then the tomatoes, and reduce until nearly dry — wet filling ruins the base.
Fold the tuna through and cool.
Line a tray with half the pastry, spread the filling, lay the sliced egg over, then top with the rest of the pastry and seal the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 200°C for 35 minutes until deep gold.

title: Tabbouleh and Hummus Bowl
description: Mostly parsley, which is the point. Ready in twenty minutes with no cooking beyond soaking the couscous.
steps: Pour the boiling stock over the couscous, cover 5 minutes, then fork through and cool.
Combine the herbs, tomato, cucumber and spring onion — the herbs should outweigh the grain, not the other way round.
Dress with the oil and lemon juice and season heavily.
Serve with hummus and warm pita.

title: Vegetable Frittata
description: Eaten hot or cold, cuts into six wedges, and keeps three days. The most useful thing you can do with a dozen eggs.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Soften the onion, zucchini and capsicum in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 10 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the parmesan and plenty of salt and pour over.
Scatter the tomatoes and feta on top and cook on the stove for 5 minutes until the edges set.
Transfer to the oven for 15 minutes until just firm in the middle.
Cool 10 minutes before cutting; tear the basil over.

title: Chicken and Corn Soup
description: A good home for leftover roast chicken. Thick, mild and reheats in two minutes.
steps: Soften the onion and celery in the butter for 8 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the potato and stock and simmer 15 minutes until the potato is soft.
Blend about a third of the soup so it thickens without losing texture.
Add the corn, chicken and cream and warm through for 5 minutes.
Finish with spring onion.

title: Teriyaki Tofu Bowl
description: Crisped tofu in a soy-mirin glaze over rice. Meat-free, high protein, and it packs into containers cleanly.
steps: Press the tofu between paper for 15 minutes, then toss in the cornflour.
Start the rice and steam the broccoli over it for the last 4 minutes.
Fry the tofu in the oil, turning only when each face has browned, about 10 minutes total.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin, honey, ginger and garlic and pour into the pan. Toss until it glazes.
Serve over rice with the broccoli, spring onion and sesame seeds.

title: Chicken Salad Sandwich
description: Yoghurt instead of most of the mayonnaise. Mix a batch and it fills sandwiches for two days.
steps: Mix the yoghurt, mayonnaise, mustard and lemon juice.
Fold the chicken, celery, spring onion and parsley through and season well.
Build sandwiches with lettuce underneath the filling — it stops the bread going wet.
To store: keep the filling in a container and build the sandwich fresh.

title: Pesto Pasta Salad
description: Cold pasta with pesto, tomatoes and mozzarella. Made in fifteen minutes and it holds two days.
steps: Cook the pasta, drain, and rinse briefly under cold water so it stops cooking.
Toss immediately with the pesto while still warm — cold pasta will not take it up.
Fold through the tomatoes, mozzarella and spinach.
Loosen with the oil and lemon juice, then add the pine nuts and parmesan.

title: Loaded Sweet Potato
description: Bake four sweet potatoes at once and top them differently each day. Almost no active work.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C, prick the sweet potatoes all over and bake 50 minutes until completely soft.
Warm the beans with the oil and spices, mashing about half of them.
Split each potato and fluff the inside with a fork.
Top with beans, cheese, yoghurt and lime juice.
Finish with spring onion and coriander.

title: Quick Egg Fried Rice
description: Ten minutes and the leftover rice is gone. The simplest possible use for yesterday's pot.
steps: Scramble the eggs quickly in half the oil and set aside.
Heat the rest of the oil, fry the garlic for 20 seconds, then add the cold rice.
Press the rice against the pan and turn it every 30 seconds until the grains separate and toast.
Return the egg, add the peas and soy sauce and toss.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onion.

title: Village Salad with Chickpeas
description: Greek salad with chickpeas folded in so it works as a meal rather than a side. No cooking at all.
steps: Combine the chickpeas, tomato, cucumber, onion and olives.
Dress with the oil, vinegar, oregano and plenty of salt.
Fold the feta through last so it stays in cubes.
To store: dress only what you are about to eat.

title: Baked Falafel Bowl
description: Baked rather than fried, so they keep two days and reheat in an oven without going greasy.
steps: Blitz the chickpeas, onion, garlic, herbs, spices and flour to a coarse paste — stop before it becomes hummus.
Chill 20 minutes, then roll into 20 balls and flatten slightly.
Brush with the oil and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes, turning once, until crusted.
Serve with hummus, cucumber, tomato and warm pita.

title: BLT Wrap
description: Ten minutes. Cook the bacon well past chewy — it stays crisp longer in a wrapped lunch.
steps: Fry the bacon until properly crisp and drain on paper.
Mix the mayonnaise and mustard and spread over the tortillas.
Salt the tomato slices and pat them dry.
Layer lettuce, tomato and bacon, then roll tightly with one end folded in.

title: Miso Noodle Soup
description: A light, quick lunch. Keep broth and noodles apart or you will find the noodles have drunk the soup.
steps: Simmer the stock with the ginger and carrot for 8 minutes.
Take the pot off the boil and whisk in the miso — boiling miso dulls it.
Add the tofu, spinach and soy sauce and warm through.
Cook the noodles separately and divide between bowls, then ladle the broth over.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onion.
